samples.summary: New write guard is client-side only; with the default config a viewer-role share link can still write the note by talking to Yorkie directly
samples.evidence: `readOnlyNoteStore` (and the design-doc text at docs/design/notes/notes.md:307-309) claims that because the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow mode, "this is the write boundary rather than a convenience in front of one". A JS Proxy in the viewer's own browser realm cannot be a boundary against the viewer, who is exactly the adversary for a viewer-role share link. Vector: open the viewer link; the page mints a Yorkie share token (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:959 `authTokenInjector={() => fetchYorkieShareToken(token)}`) and the public Yorkie key is shipped in the bundle (`VITE_YORKIE_PUBLIC_KEY`, same line region). From devtools (or a standalone @yorkie-js/sdk script) attach `note-<documentId>` with that key+token and call `doc.update(r => r.content.edit(...))`. Yorkie asks the webhook with verb `rw`; `hasAccess` correctly returns false for `link.role === 'viewer'` (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:217), but `handleAuth` converts the deny into an allow whenever `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE !== 'true'` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:111-119), which is the default. The write persists for every reader of the note. The proxy closes only the app's own code paths; it does not make the client the boundary, and documenting it as one risks the real fix (turning enforcement on) being deferred. Pre-existing shadow-mode rollout, but this delta newly rests its stated guarantee on it.

samples.summary: Access-control proxy deliberately forwards non-configurable own properties, which would hand out the raw CRDT `doc` handle if one ever existed
samples.evidence: The `get` trap returns the real value for any own data property that is non-configurable+non-writable (line 106-109), and `has`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`ownKeys` (lines 153-174) all forward non-configurable props too. The file itself names `YorkieNoteStore.doc` as "the widest hole here, reachable without so much as a method call" — so the one exception carved out of the hiding rule is exactly the shape that would leak the CRDT write handle (`doc.update()`). It is unreachable today only because TS `private readonly doc` compiles to an ordinary configurable class field; an `Object.defineProperty(this, 'doc', { value: doc })`, a decorator, or a transpiler/bundler target that emits non-configurable fields silently re-opens it, and nothing tests or asserts that invariant. The invariant that forces this exception exists only because the proxy target *is* the store: proxying an empty null-prototype object and dispatching explicitly to a captured store reference removes the exception entirely.

samples.summary: The flag the whole new store guard hangs off is derived by deny-matching one role, so any unrecognised role gets a writable handle
samples.evidence: `const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` decides whether `readOnlyNoteStore` is applied at all (notes-view.tsx:152 and editor.ts:249). `resolved.role` is an unvalidated `string` on the client (packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.ts:17), and the guard is keyed to the *deny* role rather than allow-listing the single write role (`editor`, the only other value share-link.service.ts:11 permits today). Any future or malformed role value — or a resolve response that omits `role` — yields `readOnly === false` and a fully writable CRDT store on a share-link mount. The same fail-open shape repeats in `initialize()`, where `readOnly` is a defaulted positional parameter (`readOnly = false`, editor.ts:237), so a new caller that omits it gets the unguarded store with no type error. Prefer `resolved.role !== "editor"` (fail closed) for the notes mount.

verdict.reason: Verified the full chain in-tree. read-only.ts:56-61 (and docs/design/notes/notes.md:306-309) do claim the client-side Proxy is the write boundary under the default config. The Proxy runs in the viewer's own browser realm (read-only.ts:96-175), so it cannot bind the viewer, who is the adversary for a viewer-role share link. The server-side check that would bind them is real but disabled by default: yorkie-auth.controller.ts:217 correctly denies rw for link.role !== 'editor', but handleAuth (lines 111-119) rewrites any deny into HTTP 200 / allowed:true whenever this.enforce is false, and this.enforce is YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true' (line 100-101), documented as default false (packages/backend/README.md:101; self-hosting.md:185,596 'allows everything regardless of the role'). Reachability confirmed: shared-document.tsx:955-959 ships the Yorkie project apiKey in the bundle and mints a share token via fetchYorkieShareToken, and the doc key is the deterministic note-${documentId} (shared-document.tsx:948-949), so a viewer can attach out-of-band with SDK/devtools and doc.update() the note. No guard elsewhere forces enforcement for this path — the only ENFORCE=true requirements found (template/seed/register-templates.ts:154, template-review.ts:80) gate the public template tier, not share links. In lane (authorization / access control), and the weakness is real rather than a documentation-only nit, so no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: Notes read-only is enforced only at the CodeMirror layer; the `YorkieNoteStore` handed to the engine is never wrapped, so any write that does not go through a transaction still reaches the CRDT (docs has `read-only.ts` for exactly this)
finding.evidence: `new YorkieNoteStore(doc)` is constructed identically for a viewer and an editor mount (notes-view.tsx:136) and passed straight to `initialize(..., readOnly, ...)`. The new gate is `EditorState.changeFilter` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:453), which only sees CodeMirror transactions. This diff itself demonstrates the gap: `runHistory()` needed a separate hand-written `if (readOnly) return` (editor.ts:340) precisely because `store.undo()` writes straight to the CRDT without a transaction — i.e. the filter is not the chokepoint the comment claims, it is one of two chokepoints, and the second is a per-caller check. `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:35-45` documents why docs chose a *store*-level Proxy instead: 'the server-side check behind it — the Yorkie auth webhook — ships in shadow mode by default (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`), so with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary rather than a convenience in front of one', and it deliberately allowlists readers so a member added tomorrow fails closed. `NoteStore` (packages/notes/src/store/store.ts:80-139) has 7 mutators today; the 8th added by a future change will forward to the CRDT on a viewer mount with nothing failing, while the design doc records the surface as 'inert by construction'. Attack: a viewer-role share link + any code path (existing `setLocalSelection`, a future mutator, or `EditorView.findFromDOM(el).state.facet(noteStoreFacet)` — `noteStoreFacet` is a public export of `@wafflebase/notes`, packages/notes/src/index.ts:29) writes to a document the link grants read-only.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the `YorkieNoteStore` handed to the engine is never wrapped and that read-only is enforced only at the CodeMirror layer. Both are false in this tree. `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:87` implements `readOnlyNoteStore()` — a Proxy with a reader allowlist (lines 19-27) so future mutators fail closed, no-op mutators including `setLocalSelection`, `undo`/`redo` returning null, a pass-through `batch`, nulled `getPrototypeOf`, refusing `set`/`defineProperty`/`deleteProperty`/`setPrototypeOf`/`preventExtensions`, and `has`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`ownKeys` traps that hide data fields such as `YorkieNoteStore.doc`; it is idempotent via a WeakSet. The frontend mount applies it at `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:152` (`const store = readOnly ? readOnlyNoteStore(raw) : raw;`) and passes only the wrapped handle into `initialize()` (line 155) and `storeRef` (line 116). The engine wraps independently at `packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:249`, and the guarded handle is what is published to the facet at `editor.ts:485` (`noteStoreFacet.of(store)`), which neutralizes the finding's `EditorView.findFromDOM(...).state.facet(noteStoreFacet)` vector as well. The rationale text the finding attributes solely to the docs package (auth-webhook shadow mode, reader-allowlist fail-closed reasoning) is verbatim the notes wrapper's own docblock at `read-only.ts:29-85`. Tests cover it at `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.test.ts:12-98`.

finding.summary: The viewer read-only guarantee this change builds on has no server-side enforcement in the default configuration — the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode, so every gate added here is client-side only
finding.evidence: `this.enforce = configService.get('YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE') === 'true'` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:101) defaults to false, and lines 111-119 then return ALLOW for a computed deny. `hasAccess()` would otherwise be the only thing refusing `link.role === 'viewer'` a write (line 217). Attack: a holder of a viewer-role share link calls `fetchYorkieShareToken(token)` (the frontend already does this at shared-document.tsx:959 and hands the result to the SDK), attaches with any Yorkie client outside the browser UI, and pushes arbitrary text ops to the note — no client-side `changeFilter`, `EditorState.readOnly` or `runHistory` guard is in the path. The diff's own comments (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:435-437, docs/design/notes/notes.md) acknowledge this, which makes it a known rollout state rather than a regression — but this change materially widens the surface that depends on it (a viewer is now given a live editor pane and the full `NoteEditorAPI` via the mounted toolbar), so it is worth restating that the boundary is unenforced by default. Mitigation is deployment-level (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`), not code.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element verified in the tree. yorkie-auth.controller.ts:100-101 defaults `enforce` to false when YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE is unset, and :111-119 converts any computed deny into a 200/allow ("shadow"). The viewer write refusal at :217 (needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true, with needWrite derived at :181) is therefore inert in the default configuration. The vector is reachable: auth.controller.ts:82-90 exposes an unauthenticated POST /auth/yorkie-token/share that mints a Yorkie token from any share token with no enforce-flag precondition, and shared-document.tsx:959 shows the frontend obtaining exactly that token for the SDK, so a viewer-link holder can attach an arbitrary Yorkie client and push write ops. I searched for a code-level guard requiring enforcement on this path; the only hard requirements are for the public template gallery (template-review.ts:80, seed/register-templates.ts:154-156), nothing for share links. The repo's own docs (self-hosting.md:594-598) state shadow mode "allows everything regardless of the computed decision", which confirms rather than refutes the claim. This is a server-side access-control gate that is unenforced by default, squarely in this lens's lane (weakened/missing permission gate); documentation is not a guard. No named refutation ground applies.
